source_text:
ἀναγεγραμμένων ἔστιν εἰπεῖν παν οπλίαν εἶναι τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸν Χριστόν, ὥστε ταὐτὸν
εἶναι τὸ ἐνδύσασθε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ ἐνδύ α θε τὸν Κύριον Ἰη οῦν Χρι τόν.
<εἰ> γὰρ ζώνη μέν ἐστιν ἡ ἀλήθεια θώραξ δὲ ἡ δικαιοσύνη, ὁ σωτὴρ δέ ἐστιν ἡ
ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ δικαιο ύνη, δῆλον ὅτι ὁ σωτήρ ἐστιν ἡ ζώνη καὶ ὁ θώραξ. ἀνάλογον δὲ
τούτοις αὐτὸς ἂν εἴη ἡ ἑτοιμασία τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς εἰρήνης καὶ ὁ τῆς πίστεως
θυρεὸς καὶ ἡ τοῦ σωτηρίου περικεφαλαία καὶ ἡ τοῦ πνεύματος μάχαιρα, ὅπερ ἐστὶ
ῥῆμα Θεοῦ ὁ ζῶν λόγο καὶ ἐνεργὴ καὶ τομώτερο ὑπὲρ πᾶ αν μάχαιραν δί τομον.
ποίαν δὲ κἂν ἐπινοῆσαι ἄλλην ἔστιν λέγεσθαι πανοπλίαν Θεοῦ ἣν χρὴ ἐνδύσασθαι
τὸν ἐνστησόμενον πρὸς τὰς μεθοδείας τοῦ διαβόλου ἢ τὴν ἀρετὴν ἥτις ἐστὶν ὁ
Χριστός; τοῦτον γὰρ κατὰ πάσας τὰς ἐπινοίας αὐτοῦ ἐνδυσάμενος ἱκανὸς ἔσται
στῆναι πρὸς πάσας τὰς μεθοδείας τῆς κακίας ἐνεργουμένας ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸ αὐτῆ
διαβόλου. καὶ καθὸ μὲν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἔζωσταί τις, οὐκ ἐξελκυσθήσεται ἐπὶ τὸ συγ
καταθέσθαι τοῖς ὑπὲρ τοῦ ψεύδους πιθανοῖς καὶ σοφισματώδεσι λόγοις· καθὸ δὲ τὴν
δικαιοσύνην ἠμφίεσται, ἄτρωτος ἔσται ἀπὸ τῶν βελῶν τῆς ἀδικίας, οὐδενὸς αὐτῶν
καθικνουμένου καὶ ἄδικον ποιοῦντος τὸν ἐνδεδυμένον τὴν δικαιο σύνην. καὶ ὁ
ὑποδησάμενος δὲ καλὰ ὑποδήματα τῆς ἑτοιμασίας τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς εἰρήνης, ὡς
ἕτοιμος καὶ ἑτοιμά α εἰ τὴν ἔξοδον τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο εἰρήνης ἄνθρωπος
γεγονώς, οὔτε πολεμικόν τι καὶ στασιῶδες ἐργάσεται οὔτε τοῖς ἀνετοίμοις
συγκαταδικασθήσεται. χώραν τε οὐχ ἕξει ἡ ἐχθρὰ τῇ σωτηρίᾳ τοῦ τῶν ἀνθρώπων
γένους ἀπιστία, ἔνθα ὁ τῆς πίστεως ἐστὶ θυρεός· ἄθραυστός τε διαφυλαχθήσεται τὴν
κεφαλὴν τῆς ψυχῆς, ἐν ᾗ ἐστι τὰ θεῖα καὶ νοητὰ αἰσθητήρια, ὁ τὴν περικεφαλαίαν
τοῦ σωτηρίου περικείμενος. ἀλλὰ καὶ ὡς γενναῖος στρατιώτης πάντα τὰ πολέμια τῇ
ἀληθείᾳ δόγματα κατακόψει καὶ ἀνελεῖ ὁ τὴν μάχαιραν τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅ ἐστιν ῥῆμα
Κυρίου, κρατῶν. [vi 12] ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῖν ἡ πάλη πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα, ἀλλὰ πρὸς
τὰς ἀρχάς, πρὸς τὰς ἐξουσίας, πρὸς τοὺς κοσμοκράτορας τοῦ σκότους, πρὸς τὰ
πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις. νομίζω πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα εἶναι
<πάλην> τοὺς λεγομένους παρ' αὐτῷ ἀνθρωπίνου πειρα μού , ὅτε ἡ ὰρξ ἐπιθυμοῦ α
κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματο προσ καλεῖται ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸ ποιῆσαι τὰ ἔργα αὐτῆ . οὐκέτι δὲ
ἀνθρώπινο πειρα μὸ οὐδὲ πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα ἡ πάλη, ὅτε ἤτοι ὁ Σατανᾶ
μετα χηματιζόμενο εἰ ἄγγελον φωτὸ ἀγωνίζεται ἡμᾶς πεῖσαι προσέχειν αὐτῷ ὡς
ἀγγέλῳ φωτός, ἤ τι τῶν παραπλησίων τούτοις, ἃ γίνεται ἐν πά ῃ δυνάμει καὶ ημείοι
καὶ τέρα ι ψεύδου καὶ ἐν πά ῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικία . καὶ εἰ πείσαι δέ τινα ὁ ἐχθρὸς
παραδέξασθαι αὐτὸν ὡς Κύριον ἐροῦντα ἐν αὐτῷ τάδε λέγει Κύριο , ὥστε καὶ
ὑπολαβεῖν τινα ἑαυτὸν προφήτην γεγονέναι τοῦ τῶν ὅλων Θεοῦ, ταῦτ' ἂν ποιήσαι
οὐχ ὡς αἷμα καὶ σὰρξ ἢ ἀνθρώπινο πειρα μὸ παλαίσας τῷ μέχρι τούτων ἑαυτὸν
φρουρήσαντι· διόπερ οὐδαμῶς δοτέον <τόπον> τῷ διαβόλῳ. ἐρεῖ δέ τις τὸ οὐκ ἔστιν
ἡμῖν ἡ πάλη πρὸς αἷμα καὶ σάρκα ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὰς ἀρχὰς πρὸς τὰς ἐξουσίας καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς
λέγεσθαι ἵνα διδασκώμεθα μηδὲ τὰ νομιζόμενα ἀπὸ τοῦ φρονήματο ἔρχεσθαι τῆ
αρκὸ ἡμῖν ἁμαρτήματα πρῶτον νομίζειν ἔρχεσθαι ἡμῖν ἀπὸ τῆς σαρκὸς καὶ τοῦ
αἵματος, ἀλλ' ἀπό τινων δυνάμεων ταῦτα ἐνεργουσῶν· εἰσὶ γάρ τινες δαίμονες
ἐνεργοῦντες τοὺς ἔρωτας καὶ τὰ φίλτρα, ὡς δηλοῖ καὶ ὁ προφήτης λέγων πνεύματι
πορνεία ἐπλανήθη αν. τὸ δ' ὅμοιον εἰπεῖν καὶ περὶ ἄλλων δαιμόνων θυμὸν καὶ
ὀργὴν ἐμποιούντων, οὓς ἀνακαλοῦντες καὶ οἱ περίεργοι λέγονται θυμοκάτοχ<όν>
τινα ποιεῖν. τὸ μισεῖν δὲ οὐ χωρὶς τῶν ἐνεργούντων ποιοῦμεν ὅτε μισοῦμεν
δαιμόνων· καὶ τοῦτο δέ τις ἐκ τῶν λεγομένων μισήτρων οὐκ ἀτόπως κατασκευάσει.
ἐπεὶ οὖν βούλεται, φησίν, ἡμᾶς ὁ ἀπόστολος διδάξαι οὐκ ἀπὸ τῆς φύσεως τοῦ
σώματος ἔρχεσθαι ἡμῖν τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν, διὰ τοῦτο λέγει οὐκ ἔστιν ἡμῖν ἡ πάλη πρὸς
αἷμα καὶ σάρκα, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὰς ἀρχάς, πρὸς τὰς ἐξουσίας καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. ζητοῦντες δὲ
ἀπὸ ποίων παλαιῶν ὠφελημένος γραφῶν ὁ Παῦλος ταῦτά φησιν ἀποκαλυφθεισῶν
αὐτῷ καὶ φανερωθεισῶν, στοχαζόμεθα ὅτι ἐκ τῶν ἀναγεγραμμένων περὶ πολέμων
καὶ μονομαχιῶν, οἷον τοῦ ∆αβὶδ πρὸς τὸν Γολιὰθ καὶ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς τοὺς
ἀλλοφύλους ἢ τὰ ἔθνη οἷς ἀνταγωνιζόμενοι νενικήκασιν· εἰκὸς γὰρ ἕκαστον
ἐκείνων σύμβολον εἶναι πνευματικῶν ἀρχῶν ἡττωμένων ἢ περιγινομένων. ἡ πάλη
pass_a_gloss: (... from the things about the Savior) written, it is possible to say that the full armor of God is Christ, so that 'put on the full armor of God' is the same as 'put on the Lord Jesus Christ'. For if the belt is truth and the breastplate righteousness, and the Savior is the truth and the righteousness, it is plain that the Savior is the belt and the breastplate. Analogously to these, he himself would be the readiness of the gospel of peace and the shield of faith and the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, the Word living and active and sharper than every two-edged sword. What other full armor of God could one even conceive to be meant, which the one who will stand against the methods of the devil must put on, than the virtue which is Christ? For having put him on according to all his aspects, one will be sufficient to stand against all the methods of wickedness worked by its father the devil. And insofar as one has girded on the truth, he will not be dragged toward assenting to the plausible and sophistical arguments on behalf of the lie; insofar as he has put on righteousness, he will be unwounded by the arrows of unrighteousness, none of them reaching down and making unrighteous the one clothed with righteousness. And the one who has bound on the fine shoes of the readiness of the gospel of peace, as ready and having prepared his works for the departure, and having on this account become a man of peace, will neither work anything warlike and seditious nor be condemned together with the unready. And the unbelief hostile to the salvation of the human race will have no place where the shield of faith is; and the one wearing the helmet of salvation will be kept unbroken as to the head of the soul, in which are the divine and intelligible sense-organs. But also as a noble soldier, the one holding the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of the Lord, will cut down and destroy all doctrines hostile to the truth. [6:12] 'For our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of darkness, against the spiritual things of wickedness in the heavenlies.' I think that wrestling against blood and flesh is the things called by him human temptations, when the flesh, desiring against the spirit, calls us forth to do its works. But it is no longer human temptation nor wrestling against blood and flesh, when either Satan, transforming himself into an angel of light, contends to persuade us to attend to him as to an angel of light, or something of things near these, which happen in all power and signs and wonders of falsehood and in all deceit of unrighteousness. And if the enemy should persuade someone to receive him as Lord who will say in him 'thus says the Lord', so that someone even supposes himself to have become a prophet of the God of the universe, he would do these things not as blood and flesh or human temptation, having wrestled with the one who has guarded himself up to these things; therefore by no means must place be given to the devil. Someone will say that 'our wrestling is not against blood and flesh but against the rulers, against the authorities' and what follows is said so that we be taught not to think that even the sins thought to come to us from the mind of the flesh come to us first from the flesh and the blood, but from certain powers working these. For there are certain demons working the loves and the love-philters, as the prophet also shows saying 'by a spirit of fornication they were led astray'. And the like to say also about other demons producing rage and anger, whom the meddlers (magicians) also invoking are said to make a 'thymokatochon' (anger-restraining charm). And hating we do not do without the demons working it, when we hate; and this someone will not unfittingly establish from the so-called hate-charms. Since then, he says, the apostle wishes to teach us that sinning does not come to us from the nature of the body, on this account he says 'our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities' and the rest. And seeking from what kind of ancient scriptures, revealed and made manifest to him, Paul has been helped to say these things, we conjecture that from the things recorded about wars and single combats, such as of David against Goliath and of the sons of Israel against the foreigners or the nations, contending against whom they have conquered; for it is likely that each of those is a symbol of spiritual rulers being defeated or prevailing. The wrestling (continues)
pass_b_english: written, one can say that the whole armor of God is Christ, so that "Put on the whole armor of God" is the same as "Put on the Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 13:14). For if the belt is truth and the breastplate is righteousness, and the Savior is the truth and the righteousness, it is clear that the Savior is the belt and the breastplate. In the same way he himself would be the readiness of the gospel of peace, and the shield of faith, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God: the Word who is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword (Hebrews 4:12).

What other whole armor of God could one even imagine being meant, which the one who will stand against the schemes of the devil must put on, except virtue, which is Christ? For whoever has put him on, in all his aspects, will be able to stand against all the schemes of wickedness that are worked by its father, the devil. Insofar as someone has girded himself with truth, he will not be dragged into assenting to persuasive and sophistical arguments made on behalf of falsehood. Insofar as he has clothed himself with righteousness, he will be unwounded by the arrows of unrighteousness, since none of them gets through to make the one who has put on righteousness unrighteous.

And the one who has bound on the fine shoes of the readiness of the gospel of peace, being ready and having made his works ready for the departure, and having therefore become a man of peace, will neither do anything warlike or factious nor be condemned along with the unready. Unbelief, the enemy of the salvation of the human race, will have no room where the shield of faith is. And the one who has the helmet of salvation set about his head will keep unbroken the head of the soul, where the divine senses of the mind are. More than that, like a noble soldier, the one who holds the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of the Lord, will cut down and destroy every teaching that is at war with the truth.

"For our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world rulers of the darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places" (Ephesians 6:12). I think that wrestling against blood and flesh means what he calls elsewhere human temptations (1 Corinthians 10:13), when the flesh, desiring against the spirit, calls us to do its works. But it is no longer a human temptation, nor wrestling against blood and flesh, when Satan, disguising himself as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14), strives to persuade us to heed him as an angel of light; or when something like this happens, which comes about with all power and signs and lying wonders, and with all the deceit of unrighteousness (2 Thessalonians 2:9-10).

And if the enemy should persuade someone to receive him as the Lord, who will say within him, "Thus says the Lord," so that the person even supposes he has become a prophet of the God of all things, the enemy would do this not as blood and flesh, nor as a human temptation, but as one wrestling with a man who has guarded himself up to that point. That is why no place at all must be given to the devil.

Someone will say that "Our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities," and the rest, is said to teach us not to think that even the sins which seem to come to us from the mind of the flesh come to us first from flesh and blood, but from certain powers that work them. For there are demons that work love affairs and love potions, as the prophet also shows when he says, "They were led astray by a spirit of fornication" (Hosea 4:12). The same may be said of other demons that stir up rage and anger; by calling on them, the dabblers in magic are said to make a charm for holding down anger. And when we hate, we do not hate without the demons who work hatred; one could argue this, not unreasonably, from the so-called hate charms.

"Since, then, the apostle wants to teach us," he says, "that sinning does not come to us from the nature of the body, he says for this reason, 'Our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities,' and the rest." And as we ask what ancient Scriptures, revealed and made plain to him, Paul drew on in saying this, we conjecture that it came from the accounts of wars and single combats, such as David's fight against Goliath, and the fights of the sons of Israel against the foreigners or the nations they contended with and conquered. For it is likely that each of those is a symbol of spiritual rulers being defeated or prevailing. Our wrestling

choices.why: The sentence begins at the end of u07-open ('from the things about the Savior that are'); the old English began a new sentence 'From what is written', losing 'what follows' and 'about the Savior'.

choices.term: ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασι ψεύδους
choices.english: with all power and signs and lying wonders
choices.why: 2 Thessalonians 2:9 wording; the old English garbled it.

choices.english: "Since, then, the apostle wants to teach us," he says
choices.why: φησίν marks this as the words of the 'someone' cited; the old English dropped the attribution.

choices.english: as one wrestling with a man who has guarded himself up to that point
choices.why: Keeps the participle's sense: the enemy's deceit is a wrestling with one who has so far kept guard.
